167	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
168	
169	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
170	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
171	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
172	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
173	share a root.
174	
175	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
176	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
177	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
178	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
179	
180	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
181	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
182	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
183	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.
184	
185	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
186	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
187	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
188	  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
189	  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
190	  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
191	  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`
192	  (`units-colocated-cargo-and-package-json-root-keeps-both-languages`).
193	- **U-2 (Cargo workspace folding)** A `Cargo.toml` package inside a Cargo
194	  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package
195	  (Cargo resolves the workspace as one program); it is listed in
196	  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
197	  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit

303	Config2 value spelled with a trailing `/` is refused earlier by the foundation
304	resolver's logical-path grammar and never reaches this instrument; post-reset v2
305	A-4); an empty, `.`, `..`,
306	absolute, backslash or NUL segment is `CONFIG.INVALID`
307	(`PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID`). Discovery is then restricted to exactly those
308	roots with `provenance=EXPLICIT`; an explicit root without a language marker is
309	`CONFIG.INVALID` (detail `native.explicit-root-without-marker`, exit 2), never
310	silently dropped and never widened into a scan
311	(`units-explicit-config2-workspace-root-without-marker-is-config-invalid`,
312	`units-explicit-root-dot-is-the-project-root-under-the-shared-sentinel-normalization`).
313	Security admits the custody of such a root and records the warning
314	`EXPLICIT_ROOT_WITHOUT_LANGUAGE_MARKER`; this layer decides language-unit
315	existence; the invocation terminates typed. A root inside a pruned tree has no
316	first-party marker and refuses the same way (security refuses it as
317	`JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE`). `ignorePaths` remove whole path segments and enter
318	`excludedPathPrefixes`; `entryPoints` set `entryPoints.source=explicit` (§8,
319	FR-2). No discovery output executes code, imports ambient evidence or grants
320	permission.
321	
322	**Unit scopes feed the shared scope descriptor.** `unit_scope_descriptor` emits
323	the foundation `identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/scope-descriptor`
324	(`{schemaVersion:2, workspaceRoots, pathPrefixes, excludedPathPrefixes}`; the
325	project root is spelled `.`); `excludedPathPrefixes` = Config2 `ignorePaths` ∪
326	the anchors of the pruned trees discovery observed (`prunedTrees`) ∪ the
327	conventional anchors of the shared rule (`.git`, `node_modules` under every unit
328	root; `target` under every Cargo root only) ∪ the admitted boundary anchors
329	(U-8: nested repositories, nested projects, directory-custody exclusions; the
330	boundary provenance travels beside the closed foundation record as
331	`boundaries`). `scopeDigest` is its raw SHA-256 of
332	canonical bytes under the foundation rule, and the same record is what an import
333	wrapper's `scopeDigest` names (§7). There is no native scope domain. The
334	foundation scope descriptor admits at most 1024 workspace roots; discovery's
335	4096 cap is the diagnostic population, and a project with more than 1024 unit
336	roots refuses at scope admission without truncation and asks for a narrower
337	explicit scope (§14).
338	
339	**Default discovery selects the full registered TS/JS/Rust capability set.**
340	`default_capability_selection` takes the authenticated release declaration
341	registry rows (capability × applicable language modes) and requests every
342	registered capability for every unit whose mode it applies to, `required=true`,
343	`provenance=DEFAULTED`, emitted as the foundation `analysis-spec` record. There
344	is no `preview-typescript` constant and no TypeScript-only default; a registry row
345	spelled `preview-*` is refused
346	(`units-default-capabilities-full-tsjs-rust-registry-no-preview`).
347	
348	**Backup custody join.** Dependency-source files, inert prepared rows and
349	generated-file blobs are host CAS objects under the one host storage root; they
350	inherit the identity-and-evidence §5 backup-managed-storage choice
351	(`--allow-backup-custody` or an admitted storage-policy record; CI without a
352	choice refuses `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `storage.backup-choice-required`).
353	Native adds no second store and no custody rule of its own.
354	
355	`mixed-native-partial` fixes the meaning: TypeScript unit complete, co-located Rust
356	unit missing an external crate → TypeScript-scoped predicates evaluate;
357	repository-scoped semantic predicates are indeterminate with
358	`input-closure-incomplete` naming the crate; syntax and clone predicates complete
359	for both.

363	## 2. Semantic universe successors
364	
365	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
366	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
367	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
368	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
369	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
370	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,
371	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
372	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
373	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.
374	Input-adapter observation sequences retain their own declared order; a producer
375	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.
376	
377	### 2.1 `rust-v2` (replaces `rust-v1.resolvedInputs`)
378	
379	All `rust-v1` release/toolchain identity fields are retained unchanged.
380	`resolvedInputs` becomes `RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`:
381	
382	| Field | Type | Rule |
383	|---|---|---|
384	| `schemaVersion` | `2` | exact integer |
385	| `edition` | per-package map `{packageKey: 2015\|2018\|2021\|2024}` | keys sorted; every workspace member present |
386	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{path:"Cargo.lock", contentSha256, lockfileVersion∈{3,4}}` | absence is `input-closure-incomplete` (`lockfile-missing`), never an implicit `cargo generate-lockfile` |
387	| `dependencySourceSetId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of the admitted `DependencySourceSetV1` (§3) |
388	| `unifiedFeaturesId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of `UnifiedFeaturesV1` (§3.4) |
389	| `nativeContextId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of `NativeContextV2` (§2.3) |
390	| `cfgSets` | array of `{cfgSetId, cfg}` length 1..4 | default `[primary, primary+test]`; extra sets are Plan-bound. Every set's `cfg` **contains every member of the context's `baseCfg`**: sets differ from the base only by additions, and `cfgSetId` is unique within the universe. A set that dropped a base cfg would analyse a configuration nothing selected |
391	| `rustflags` | `RustflagsProjectionV1` | the *honored* and *stripped* flag lists after the exact allowlist (§3.3); equal to the bound context's `configProjection.rustflags` |
392	| `crateRootPaths` | sorted unique canonical paths | unchanged; every path must be in the analysed snapshot inventory |
393	| `configProjectionSha256` | `DigestHex` | the 64-hex suffix of `H("native.cargo-config-projection.v2", CargoConfigProjectionV2)` over the bound context's `configProjection` (§3.3). It is **not** the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes, and **not** `CargoConfigProjectionV2.projectionSha256`, which is the raw digest of the projected config *file*. Raw file digests are also in the snapshot |
394	| `preparedResolution` | `none \| host-prepared \| imported-inert` | how prepared products entered the universe (R4) |
395	| `executionCapableResolution` | boolean | `preparedResolution ≠ none`. It names the **meaning** of the universe (resolution consumed inert products of some execution). It is **never** a host execution grant: the grant is the operational `RepoExecutionGrantV2` reference outside Plan (§5.1). `imported-inert` needs only `read-import` in the semantic grant; only `host-prepared` projects `prepare-code` |
396	| `preparedOutputSetId` | `Sha256Text \| null` | identity of the admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3`; `null` when `preparedResolution=none` |
397	
398	Change rule: any field change changes PlanId. Missing, unknown, float-spelled,
399	unordered or handshake-mismatched values fail before provider execution.
400

400	
401	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its
402	admitted context before PlanId, exactly as `typescript-v2` is bound by
403	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
404	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it
405	executes no cargo, rustc, build script, proc macro or filesystem read — and takes
406	the admitted context descriptor, the retained nested input records
407	(`DependencySourceSetV1`, `UnifiedFeaturesV1`, `PreparedOutputSetV3` when one is
408	selected) and the analysed snapshot inventory. All three are **required**: there is
409	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,
410	and omission is the typed refusal `native.universe-retained-inputs-not-supplied`,
411	never an ADMIT. It refuses when
412	
413	- the admission is not a Rust context admission, or the universe names a context
414	  this host did not mint, or the supplied context bytes are not the admitted ones;
415	- any overlapping field disagrees:
416	  `dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId`, `preparedOutputSetId`, `rustflags`,
417	  `configProjectionSha256`, `executionCapableResolution`, `preparedResolution`, or a
418	  `cfgSets` entry that drops a base cfg or repeats a `cfgSetId`;
419	- a nested semantic identity is not the exact H identity of the retained record of
420	  its registered domain, or that record contradicts the universe or context —
421	  a dependency set whose `lockfileIdentity` differs, unified features computed for
422	  another `targetTriple` or resolver version, or a prepared set bound to another
423	  dependency set, toolchain, cfg set or preparation kind;
424	- a prepared output set is retained but **no** universe selected it
425	  (`preparedOutputSetId = null`): optional absent preparation stays absent, and
426	  bytes in custody never enter a resolution by being in custody;
427	- the snapshot does not contain what the universe names: `Cargo.lock` missing or
428	  with different bytes, a `crateRootPaths` entry not inventoried, or a
429	  `replacedSnapshotConfigs` entry not inventoried.
430	
431	`executionCapableResolution` remains a statement about what the resolution
432	consumed, never an execution grant; retained inert prepared bytes cannot imply one,
433	and the operational `RepoExecutionGrantV2` reference stays outside Plan (§5.1).

435	### 2.2 `typescript-v2` (replaces `typescript-v1.resolvedInputs`)
436	
437	Retained **in the universe**: `tsconfigGraphHash`, `programRootFiles`,
438	`executionCapableResolution` (constant `false`: no TypeScript-side repository
439	execution is selected).
440	
441	**Relocated to the context** (§2.4), and therefore *not* fields of the closed
442	`TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`, which is `additionalProperties: false`:
443	`compilerOptions` — now `TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2.honoredOptions` and
444	`strippedOptions`; `packageLockIdentity` — now
445	`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.lockfileIdentity`, with `lockfileKind` retained in the
446	universe as its kind projection; and `resolvedNodeModulesLayout` — now the
447	retained `ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1` record that
448	`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.nodeModulesLayoutDigest` names. An implementer building
449	a universe record from the older "Retained:" list produced a record that fails
450	admission; these three moved, they were not dropped.
451	
452	`tsconfigGraphHash` is the **raw SHA-256 of `C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1)`** — a
453	retained canonical record, not an H identity and not an opaque id. That record is
454	`{schemaVersion: 1, entryConfigPath, nodes}`, where `nodes` is the strictly ascending
455	unique-by-`path` array of every config file actually read, each
456	`{path, contentSha256, kind, extendsResolved}`: `contentSha256` is that file's
457	inventoried snapshot digest and `extendsResolved` is the ordered array of
458	project-relative paths its `extends` entries resolved to. Later entries take
459	precedence; repetitions are retained, and an empty array means no base config.
460	`entryConfigPath` selects the root config, or is null for synthesized configuration.
461	The record is a **required** binding input, and the binding
462	checks that `nodes[].path` is exactly the context's
463	`configProjection.configGraphPaths` set, that every node's digest is the snapshot's,
464	and that every edge names another node. Every node must be reachable from the
465	selected entry and the graph must be acyclic, so the universe key and the context
466	cannot describe two different config graphs.
467	
468	`configOrigin` is **derived from that retained record, never asserted**:
469	`synthesized` exactly when the entry is null and `nodes` is empty; otherwise it
470	comes from the selected entry's kind (`jsconfig` for a jsconfig entry, otherwise
471	`tsconfig`). Node kind agrees with its path as specified by the schema and native
472	admission. A jsconfig entry extending a shared base remains a jsconfig program.
473	The universe's `configOrigin` must equal the derived value. This is the input
474	§2.4's agreement check needs; without the record the `tsconfig`/`jsconfig`
475	distinction was not derivable and two spellings minted two universe identities for
476	one admitted context.
477	
478	Added: `schemaVersion=2`, `languageMode`, `configOrigin`,
479	`synthesizerVersion`, `synthesizedOptions`, `packageModuleType`, `allowJs`,
480	`checkJs`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled`,
481	`resolutionCompletenessImplied=false`, `jsRootFiles`, `lockfileKind`,
482	`nodeModulesInReadSet` (`false` means bare specifiers are
483	`unresolved-module-specifier`, scope `external`; never an implicit install) and

489	**`ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1`** is the record that digest names, and it is what
490	makes the ordinary TypeScript project — the one with dependencies — representable.

520	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
521	
522	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
523	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
524	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
525	own language and refuses the other.
526	
527	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
528	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
529	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
530	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
531	
532	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
533	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
534	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
535	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
536	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
537	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
538	descriptor and tree.
539	
540	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
541	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
542	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
543	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
544	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
545	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a
546	platform family has no bundled linker in the closure, in-host preparation is
547	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
548	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.
549	
550	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
551	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
552	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).
553	
554	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)
555	
556	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
557	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
558	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,
559	nodeModulesLayoutDigest|null, lockfileIdentity|null}`.
560	
561	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,
562	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],
563	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.
564	
565	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
566	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
567	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
568	
569	| Field | Produced from |
570	|---|---|
571	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
572	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
573	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
574	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. A missing row refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<name>`, because an alternate partial declaration inventory for the same retained library is not the required complete record. A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
575	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` names the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must be covered by a retained component |
576	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
577	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
578	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). Stripping is disclosed here and is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else. `typeAcquisitionEnabled` and `executableSelected` are schema constants `false` |
579	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
580	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |
581	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{kind, path, contentSha256}` of the admitted lockfile, or `null` when `lockfileKind=none` |
582	
583	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
584	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
585	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
586	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
587	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
588	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
589	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
590	
591	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
592	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
593	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
594	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
595	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
596	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
597	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
598	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
599	
600	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
601	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
602	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
603	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
604	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
605	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
606	
607	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
608	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
609	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
610	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
611	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
612	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
613	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
614	the admitted id refuse
615	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
616	
617	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
618	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
619	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
620	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
621	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
622	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
623	
624	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
625	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
626	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no case-insensitive duplicate names,
627	and selects the same case-insensitive name set as the honored `lib` list;
628	each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
629	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
630	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
631	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
632	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
633	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
634	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
635	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
636	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
637	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
638	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
639	DomainDetail codes.
640	
641	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
642	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is
643	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze.

669	## 3. Sealed dependency inputs (AR-07)
670	
671	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
672	
673	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
674	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
675	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
676	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
677	
678	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
679	
680	| Field | Rule |
681	|---|---|
682	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
683	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
684	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
685	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
686	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
687	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
688	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
689	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
690	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
691	
692	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
693	
694	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
695	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
696	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
697	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
698	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
699	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
700	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
701	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
702	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
703	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
704	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
705	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
706	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
707	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
708	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
709	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
710	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
711	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
712	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
713	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
714	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
715	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
716	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
717	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
718	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
719	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
720	  syntax analysis.
721	
722	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
723	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
724	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
725	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

727	### 3.2 Custody and transport
728	
729	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
730	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
731	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
732	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
733	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
734	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
735	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.

737	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
738	
739	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
740	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
741	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
742	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
743	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
744	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
745	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
746	
747	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
748	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
749	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
750	
751	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
752	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
753	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
754	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.
755	- **CC-2** `CARGO_HOME` is a fresh private empty directory created for the
756	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.
757	- **CC-3** The constructed environment contains no `PATH`, `CARGO_*`, `RUSTFLAGS`,
758	  `RUSTC*`, `RUSTDOC*`, `RUSTUP_*`, `CC`/`CXX`/`LD`/`AR`/`TARGET_*` variables;
759	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
760	  paths on the command line, not via environment.
761	- **CC-4** Every selected tool digest equals its entry in `ToolClosureV1`.
762	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
763	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
764	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.
765	
766	Projected (honored) keys: `build.target`, `build.rustflags`,
767	`target.<triple>.rustflags` (both through the flag allowlist below),
768	`source.<name>.directory` pointing inside the snapshot with `replace-with`,
769	`resolver`, and `[patch]` in `Cargo.toml`. Stripped and recorded: `alias`,
770	`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `build.rustc-workspace-wrapper`,
771	`build.rustdoc`, `build.target-dir`, `build.build-dir`, `build.incremental`,
772	`build.dep-info-basedir`, `cargo-new`, `credential-alias`, `doc`, `env`,
773	`future-incompat-report`, `http`, `install`, `net`, `patch` (config-level),
774	`profile`, `registries`, `registry`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`,
775	`target.*.<links>`, `term`, `unstable`. A `[source]` replacement pointing outside
776	the snapshot is `input-closure-incomplete` (`source-replacement-outside-snapshot`).
777	
778	**Two distinct digests, both now named.** `CargoConfigProjectionV2.projectionSha256`
779	is the raw SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the **single projected `.cargo/config.toml`
780	file** the adapter materializes under CC-5 — a raw artifact digest of a file.
781	`rust-v2.configProjectionSha256` (§2.1) is the 64-hex suffix of
782	`H("native.cargo-config-projection.v2", CargoConfigProjectionV2)` over the whole
783	projection record. Neither is the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes, and
784	neither substitutes for the other. Every `replacedSnapshotConfigs` entry names a
785	path that must be in the analysed snapshot inventory: the originals remain snapshot
786	bytes for identity even though Cargo never reads them.
787	
788	**Rustflags allowlist** (`RustflagsProjectionV1`; primary source
789	`doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/command-line-arguments.html`, read 2026-09-06). Honored,
790	exactly:
791	
792	| Flag | Constraint |
793	|---|---|
794	| `--cfg <ident>` / `--cfg <ident>="<value>"` / `--cfg=<…>` | identifier syntax; no spaces |
795	| `-A/-W/-D/-F <lint>`, `-A<lint>`… and long forms; `--cap-lints <allow\|warn\|deny\|forbid>` | lint name syntax `[a-z0-9_:]+` |
796	| `-C target-feature=…`, `-C target-cpu=…`, `-C opt-level=…`, `-C debuginfo=…`, `-C panic=…`, `-C overflow-checks=…`, `-C debug-assertions=…`, `-C strip=…` | value matches `[A-Za-z0-9_+,.=-]+` |

826	### 3.6 `PreparedOutputSetV3`: inert rows only (feedback 4, R2)
827	
828	Domain `native.prepared-output-set.v3` (revised in place; v3 was never accepted).
829	`{schemaVersion:3, preparation: {kind: authorized-execution|imported-descriptor,
830	authorizationId|null, importId|null, toolchain, dependencySourceSetId, cfgSetId,
831	producer}, rows: [PreparedOutputRowV3…]}`.
832	
833	`PreparedOutputRowV3`: `{kind, ownerKey, configuration, site|null, generated|null,
834	inputBinding: {ownerFileManifestSha256, dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest,
835	cfgSetId}, blob: {sha256, byteLength, mediaType}, status: ok|failed,
836	failureDetail|null}`.
837	
838	- **PO-0 (inert by kind and consumption channel; a media type is a label, never a
839	  trust proof)** Admissible row kinds are exactly three:
840	  `build-script-directives` (`text/x-cargo-directives`: the captured `cargo:`
841	  lines, including `rustc-cfg`/`rustc-env` consumed by `cfg`/`env!`),
842	  `macro-expansion` (`text/x-rust-expansion`: the fully expanded token text for one
843	  invocation `site` = `{path, startByte, endByte, inputTokenDigest}`), and
844	  `generated-file` (`generated = {logicalPath, blob}` with media type
845	  `text/x-rust-source`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`: one data file
846	  a build script wrote under `OUT_DIR`). Row kinds `proc-macro-dylib` and
847	  `build-script-binary` are refused **regardless of the media type they claim**
848	  (a dylib relabelled `text/x-rust-expansion` is still a dylib row), and a media
849	  type outside the kind's set is refused; either is
850	  `native.prepared-output-not-inert` (exit 2), from an import *and* from the
851	  in-host step alike (`generated-file-media-type-is-not-trust-proof-kind-decides`).
852	  **No prepared artifact is ever loaded, linked or executed by the semantic
853	  worker.** Expansions are looked up by exact
854	  `(path, span, inputTokenDigest, macro crate manifest)`; a miss is a
855	  `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge (L-RS4).
856	- **PO-4 (generated-file input closure and the read-only virtual `OUT_DIR`)**
857	  The worker resolves `env!("OUT_DIR")` for owner *O* to the read-only virtual
858	  path `.opensip/out/v1/<ownerKey>/` in its sealed VFS. A site
859	  `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs"))` (likewise
860	  `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) reads the `generated-file` row bound to
861	  `(ownerKey, logicalPath="generated.rs")` whose `inputBinding` equals the current
862	  context, and consumes its bytes **only** as Rust source text, a string literal or
863	  a byte literal respectively. A miss (no row, stale binding, failed owner) is a
864	  typed unknown: `build-script-generated-unavailable` edge, cause
865	  `generated-file-missing`; it is never a hard failure and never a fallback to a
866	  host path (`generated-file-include-out-dir-resolves-inert`,
867	  `generated-file-missing-is-typed-unknown-not-failure`). Strict bounds
868	  (`GeneratedInputBoundsV1`): `logicalPath` is a strict relative path (no `/`
869	  prefix, no `.`/`..` segment, no NUL or backslash, ≤ 1024 bytes; an escaping path
870	  fails exact typed admission and the worker lookup independently refuses it with
871	  cause `generated-file-out-of-bounds`), `maxGeneratedFilesPerOwner 4096`,
872	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
873	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to
874	  archive members by exact `blobs[]` digest; an archive member outside the
875	  wrapper's `blobs` is never read (`generated-file-path-escape-and-bounds-refused`).
876	- **PO-1 (staleness)** A row is usable only if `inputBinding` equals the current
877	  context (owner manifest, dependency set, toolchain digest, cfg set). A stale row
878	  is refused before Plan construction (`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, detail
879	  `native.stale-prepared-output`, listing the differing fields) when prepared mode
880	  was selected explicitly, or is ignored with a disclosed `staleRows` list and
881	  non-prepared fallback when prepared mode was defaulted. It never uses a stale blob.
882	- **PO-2 (failed rows)** A `failed` build script is retained as a row so the same
883	  inputs need not be re-run; the owner is analyzed non-prepared
884	  (`build-script-generated-unavailable`).
885	- **PO-3 (imported)** An imported set carries the same binding fields and
886	  `provenanceAssurance: declared`; the host cannot verify that an external
887	  preparer produced the expansions faithfully. Facts derived from them are
888	  Plan-bound and disclosed with the import identity and producer.
889	
890	Where do the expansions and generated files come from? From the **preparation
891	step** (§5.3), which is the only place proc-macro dylibs are built and loaded and
892	build scripts run, inside the authorized `repository-code` principal with live
893	boundaries. The step captures the required generated **data** and discards every
894	executable product; its output is the inert row set, and the worker consumes only
895	that.

899	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
900	
901	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
902	
903	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
904	
905	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
906	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
907	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
908	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
909	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
910	   "Could we see every consumer?"
911	
912	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
913	
914	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
915	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
916	
917	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
918	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
919	
920	```
921	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
922	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
923	```
924	
925	where `D` is the closed foundation record
926	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
927	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
928	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
929	
930	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
931	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
932	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
933	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
934	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
935	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
936	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
937	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
938	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
939	
940	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
941	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
942	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
943	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
944	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
945	against a value the provider never supplied.
946	
947	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
948	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
949	
950	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
951	   commitment is never an input to this step.
952	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
953	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
954	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
955	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
956	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
957	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
958	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
959	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
960	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
961	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
962	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
963	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
964	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
965	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
966	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
967	
968	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
969	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
970	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
971	
972	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
973	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
974	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
975	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
976	
977	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
978	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
979	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
980	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
981	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
982	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
983	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
984	
985	Cases: `subject-scope-commitment-is-the-scope2-identity-in-native-sha256-text-form`,
986	`subject-scope-commitment-binds-the-snapshot-not-only-the-subject-list`,
987	`coverage-admission-mints-coverage2-from-the-host-subject-scope`,
988	`coverage-commitment-chosen-by-the-claimant-is-refused`,
989	`coverage-producer-chosen-narrower-examined-partition-is-refused`,
990	`coverage-examined-subject-count-that-disagrees-with-the-enumeration-is-refused`,
991	`coverage-key-naming-a-universe-outside-the-host-scope-is-refused`,
992	`coverage-complete-claimed-over-an-admitted-unresolved-edge-is-refused-at-the-boundary`,
993	`coverage-incomplete-over-an-exhaustive-partition-admits-with-the-same-commitment`,
994	`coverage-use-requires-the-subject-scope-to-be-in-the-evaluated-view`,
995	`coverage2-whose-subject-scope-is-outside-the-view-is-refused`,
996	`coverage2-never-admitted-at-the-producer-boundary-is-refused-in-a-view`,

998	`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`. The two positive coverage cases

1000	digest and the canonical payload rather than pinning a literal, so a schema-document edit moves the
1001	identity visibly instead of silently invalidating a frozen value.

1003	**Coordination (identity owner).** Identity §3 now states the same recipe in its own words —
1004	`subjectScopeCommitment` is `"sha256:"` plus the 64-hex suffix of the admitted `scope2` identity,
1005	"another textual form of the **same** digest, not a separate hash of the subjects or of the scope

1017	`resolutionCompleteness.state=incomplete`; the predicate reports
1018	`resolution-incomplete` and `foo`/`bar` are both marked affected (§4.5). Both
1019	behaviors are executable in the reference model (`computed-access-m-k`, v1 oracle

1022	### 4.2 Requirement v2
1023	
1024	`RequirementV2` (closed): `{relation, minResolution, minConfidenceMillionths
1025	(default 0), completeness: complete|partial-ok, quantifier:
1026	existential|universal-negative, unresolvedEdgePolicy: forbid|disclose,
1027	externalConsumerPolicy: forbid|assume-closed, derivationPolicy: any|declared-only
1028	(relation `types` only), scope?}`.
1029	
1030	- `quantifier=universal-negative` requires `completeness=complete`.
1031	- A repair prerequisite, a `no-consumer`/`cold-code`/`unreachable` authoritative
1032	  finding, and any predicate whose truth is a negative over consumers **must** use

1146	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.

1149	2. Rung below `minResolution` → the rung-unavailable cause (`language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`) else `required-relation-missing`.

1198	
1199	The security contract S10 registers principal class `repository-code`

1200	(`RepoExecutionGrantV2`, execution classes `build-script | proc-macro |
1201	test-runner`). One principal, three current spellings, joined explicitly and
1202	checked by schema constants:
1203	
1204	| Where | Spelling | Role |
1205	|---|---|---|
1206	| security S10 / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.principalClass` | `repository-code` | principal class of the admitted grant |
1207	| foundation `identity-schemas.v2#semantic-grant.principals[].kind` / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.semanticGrantPrincipalKind` | `trusted-repository-code` | Plan-bound semantic projection `{kind, closureId (tool closure), ownerSourceDigest (owner file manifest)}` with `analysisOperations ∋ prepare-code` |

1211	(`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)`, the workflow's `securityGrantRef`):
1212	it is excluded from the Plan descriptor and from every content identity
1213	(`authorized-execution-interactive-with-declared-owner-disclosed` checks
1214	`authorizationRefInPlan=false`). The **semantic grant projection** is what the Plan
1215	binds. A universe with `preparedResolution=imported-inert` projects only
1216	`read-import`; only `host-prepared` projects `prepare-code`. Prepared semantic
1217	availability therefore never implies that this host holds or held an execution
1218	grant (`prepared-imported-inert-implies-no-host-execution-grant`).

1220	The principal, identified by `{projectId, snapshotId, ownerKey,
1221	ownerFileManifestSha256, toolchainDigest}`, is **outside** the first-party TCB.
1222	Executing it in-host is a disclosed trusted-code execution of code the user chose
1223	to analyze; OpenSIP does not vouch for it and does not confine it unless a
1224	platform primitive is enforced. The security owner supplies the revocation clock
1225	and cancellation carrier (H-2).

1230	`rust-v2.executionCapableResolution` via `preparedOutputSetId`: `{schemaVersion:2,
1231	operation:"native.prepare", principalClass:"repository-code", projectId,
1232	snapshotId (snapshot2), dependencySourceSetId, toolchain, toolClosure, cfgSetId,
1233	owners: [{ownerKey, kind: build-script|proc-macro, ownerFileManifestSha256,

1245	JSON output: "Build scripts and procedural macros from N packages will run with

1258	### 5.3 What the preparation step does (feedback 4)
1259	
1260	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
1261	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
1262	
1263	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
1264	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
1265	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
1266	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
1267	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
1268	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
1269	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
1270	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
1271	   nothing is installed).
1272	3. **Inside this same authorized step**, drive the bundled compiler's expansion
1273	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
1274	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,
1275	   and capture the expanded token text per site as `macro-expansion` rows; capture
1276	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
1277	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the
1278	   principal, with the live boundaries, and nowhere else.
1279	4. **Capture required generated data, discard executable products** (R2). For
1280	   each build-script owner: capture the `cargo:` directive lines as a
1281	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
1282	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
1283	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
1284	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under
1285	   `OUT_DIR` within the PO-4 bounds; discard the build-script binary, every
1286	   dylib/object/archive/executable product and unreferenced scratch files; discard
1287	   the proc-macro dylibs. Referenced paths the script did not produce are recorded
1288	   (`missingReferencedPaths`) and become typed unknowns at analysis. Nothing of
1289	   `OUT_DIR` survives except the captured data rows
1290	   (`preparation-capture-keeps-referenced-data-discards-executable-products`).
1291	   The result is `PreparedOutputSetV3` (`kind: authorized-execution`).
1292	
1293	The semantic worker then consumes the inert set through the protocol
1294	(`PreparedOutputManifest/Chunk/Seal`), looks up expansions by exact site key, and
1295	executes nothing. `RepositoryResolutionV3.workerExecutesRepositoryCode` is the
1296	constant `false`. An external preparer may supply the same inert shape
1297	(`kind: imported-descriptor`, `declared` provenance, §3.6 PO-3); it can never
1298	supply a dylib.

1303	|---|---|
1304	| Owner build script exits non-zero | row `failed`; other owners continue; owner analyzed non-prepared |

1325	### 6.1 Modes and evidence levels
1326	
1327	| Mode | Level/algorithm | Evidence level (closed) | Authority |
1328	|---|---|---|---|
1329	| `exact` | `L0-verbatim` | `byte-identical` | fact |
1330	| `normalized` | `L1-lexical` (default) or `L2-comment-insensitive` (opt-in) | `lexically-identical` / `comment-insensitive-identical` | fact |
1331	| `structural` | `L3-identifier-insensitive` | `identifier-insensitive-identical` | fact |
1332	| `near` | `near-v1`: Jaccard over 5-gram shingles of the L3 token stream | `similar-candidate` | candidate only |
1333	| `cross-tsjs` | `tsjs-erasure-v1` projection, then L3 | `cross-language-syntax-candidate` / `excluded` | candidate only |
1334	
1335	No semantic equivalence is inferred by any mode.

1337	### 6.2 Parameters (selected)
1338	
1339	`minOccurrences 2`; `minBodyBytes 64` (exact); `minTokens 20` (L1–L3,
1340	cross-tsjs); `minTokens 50` (near); `nearThreshold 800000` millionths;

1343	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
1344	
1345	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
1346	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
1347	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
1348	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
1349	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
1350	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
1351	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
1352	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
1353	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
1354	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
1355	
1356	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
1357	|---|---|---|---|
1358	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
1359	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
1360	
1361	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
1362	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
1363	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.

1365	### 6.4 TS/JS cross-language decision (feedback 9)
1366	
1367	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
1368	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
1369	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
1370	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
1371	
1372	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
1373	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
1374	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
1375	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.

1377	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),
1378	  value-bearing `namespace`, decorators, `import =`. A body containing any of them
1379	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason

1382	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema
1383	  constants. A cross candidate is never a baseline member, never a Control input,

1386	Cases: `clone-cross-tsjs-candidate-only`, `clone-cross-tsjs-runtime-significant-excluded`.

1536	
1537	### 9.1 Versions and identity negotiation (feedback 1)
1538	
1539	`rust-semantic` protocol major **3**; `typescript-semantic` protocol major **2**.
1540	Capability tokens (closed, `CapabilityToken`): identity tokens
1541	`source-identity-snapshot2`, `plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`,
1542	`coverage-v3`; plus `sealed-vfs-v1`, `multi-stage-analyze-v1`,
1543	`<lang>-semantic-facts-v1`, `resolution-completeness-v2`, `unresolved-edge-v1`,
1544	`dependency-source-v1` (Rust), `prepared-output-v3` (Rust), `native-context-v2`.
1545	`HelloV3` also carries `identityVersions: {snapshot:2, plan:2, fact:2, coverage:3}`
1546	and `HelloAckV3` must echo it exactly.
1547	
1548	Reject-before-disclosure ordering:
1549	
1550	1. **Plan time (no spawn).** The host reads the signed capability row. The four
1551	   identity tokens are required for every worker; a row lacking any of them, or
1552	   any token the Plan needs, is never spawned: affected Coverage keys are
1553	   `unknown / provider-unavailable` (cause `capability-missing`). No raw
1554	   `snapshot2`, `plan2` or source byte reaches a worker that cannot name them
1555	   (`negotiation-v1-only-worker-never-spawned`).
1556	2. **Hello → HelloAck (no source bytes).** Exact recursive equality of the token
1557	   array and identity versions; mismatch → `FAULT`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`,
1558	   no snapshot, dependency or prepared byte is ever written.
1559	3. **OpenUniverse** carries `snapshot2`, `plan2`, the universe descriptor
1560	   including `nativeContext`, and `RepositoryResolutionV3`. The host state
1561	   machine admits it only when `identityNegotiated=true`; otherwise the run faults
1562	   with `sourceBytesSent=false` (`protocol3-open-universe-without-identity-faults`).
1563	4. Snapshot custody, dependency-source custody, prepared custody,
1564	   `NativeContextVerified`, then Analyze.
1565	
1566	Existing V1 relation payload grammars are reused unchanged inside `fact2` by
1567	exact `payloadSchemaDigest`; legacy FACT-ID-V1 identities remain historical and
1568	are never relabeled.
