1684	
1685	All are `H(domain, descriptor)` under the foundation recipe, hex-encoded as
1686	`sha256:<64 hex>` where a `Sha256Text` is required:
1687	`native.semantic-universe.rust.v2`, `native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2`,
1688	`native.context.rust.v2`, `native.context.typescript.v2`, `native.dependency-source-set.v1`,
1689	`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, `native.unified-features.rust.v1`,
1690	`native.cargo-config-projection.v2` (over `CargoConfigProjectionV2`, §3.3 — the
1691	domain `rust-v2.configProjectionSha256` carries the suffix of),
1692	`native.prepared-output-set.v3`, `native.authorized-execution.v2`,
1693	`native.clone-suppression.v1`, `native.framework-recognition.v1`,
1694	`native.workspace-unit.v1`, `native.entry-points.v1`,
1695	`native.source-unit-ownership.v1` (over `SourceUnitOwnershipV1`, §2.1 — the
1696	committed source-path to compilation-target relation, its closed target table and
1697	its explicit selection), `native.compilation-unit.v1` (over `UnitIdentityV1`, the
1698	published four-field preimage a `unitId` is `H` of), and the two native import
1699	payload domains `native.import-payload.{dependency-source,prepared-output}.v1`
1700	(registry spelling, §7.1). Runtime/test/history payload domains are the workflow
1701	owner's; the former native `runtime-coverage`/`test-results`/`history` payload
1702	domains are withdrawn (their records are adapter input shapes, never payloads).
1703	Import identity itself is the foundation `import` domain (`import2:`), not a
1704	native domain; the import wrapper's auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 records,
1705	not domains. `subjectScopeCommitment` adds **no** native domain: it is the foundation
1706	`subject-scope` identity in a different textual form (§4.1a).
1707	
1708	**Three admitted textual forms of one digest, and when each is required.** They are not
1709	alternative recipes; the preimage and the `H` frame are always the foundation's.
1710	
1711	| Form | Where it is required | Example |
1712	|---|---|---|
1713	| foundation typed prefix `<prefix>:<64 hex>` | any foundation identity field: `snapshot2:`, `plan2:`, `closure2:`, `scope2:`, `coverage2:`, `import2:` | `scope2:2c5f…` |
1714	| native `Sha256Text` `sha256:<64 hex>` | any native record field typed `Sha256Text`, where the foundation domain is not carried in-band: `nativeContextId`, `dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId`, `preparedOutputSetId`, `CoverageKeyV2.subjectScopeCommitment` | `sha256:2c5f…` |
1715	| bare `DigestHex` (64 hex, no prefix) | raw SHA-256 digests and 64-hex **suffixes of a typed foundation identity**: `plan.nativeContextDigests`, `sourceUniverse`/`targetUniverse`, `configProjectionSha256`, `typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot`, `rustcDevLlvmDigest` | `2c5f…` |
1716	
1717	A suffix field is bare precisely because its typed prefix belongs to the foundation identity
1718	it was taken from; admission recovers that identity by re-prefixing and requires a retained
1719	closure to match (§2.3, §2.4). The textual form is a spelling, not an annotation:
1720	which recipe a field carries is what that field's own `x-opensip-digest`
1721	annotation says, and no prefix implies one.
1722	
1723	**Language-version binding for FACT-IDENTITY body frames.** A `clones` relation
1724	payload's `bodyIdentity` is framed with a `languageId` and a `languageVersion`
1725	that the inherited `fact-identity-policy.v2` requires to be "canonical identity
1726	bytes supplied by ResolvedInputs/PlanId, not a human display string", for "the
1727	provider interpreting the body span". The identity that satisfies it is the
1728	**compiler**, and it is already committed: a universe's own `nativeContextId` —
1729	a reference Run closure already requires to be Plan-selected — reaches the
1730	admitted retained context, whose `toolchain` carries `rustcVersion` and
1731	`rustCommitHash` here, and `compilerName`, `compilerVersion` and
1732	`compilerPackageDigest` for TypeScript. §2.3's admission already refuses
1733	`native.native-context-compiler-version-not-from-manifest` unless that version
1734	equals the admitted tool closure's `semanticVersion`, for both languages, so the
1735	binding inherits a real chain from a retained closure manifest rather than
1736	copying a display string. **Following an existing admitted reference needs no new
1737	universe field**, and none was added.
1738	
1739	The binding lives in the universe domain rows at
1740	`foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/domainSets/native-semantic-universe/*/languageVersionBinding`,
1741	and it names, per language, the exact source path of every field of the closed
1742	`body-language-version` record plus each **excluded** field with its reason. The
1743	boundary is: what identifies the component that **interprets the body span**, and
1744	the selected source **dialect**. Not the operational platform (`targetTriple`,
1745	`hostTriple`), not the resolution environment (`sysrootDigest`,
1746	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`, `libSelection`), not the code-generation
1747	backend (`rustcDevLlvmDigest`), not build or dependency tooling (`cargoVersion`,
1748	`resolverVersion`), not paths (`crateRootPaths`), and not option synthesis
1749	(`languageMode`, `synthesizerVersion`), which describes how a program was
1750	assembled rather than which language read the body.
1751	
1752	`edition` is a map from crate **name** to year, so it is the *selected value*
1753	that is the dialect, never the map: a body identity that varied with unrelated
1754	crates would be neither meaningful nor representable. When the map's distinct
1755	value set has exactly one member — the ordinary case, including a large
1756	single-edition workspace — that member is the dialect of every body and no owner
1757	selection arises. When it has more than one, the **owning compilation unit
1758	decides**.
1759	
1760	More precisely, the **compilation target** decides, not the package. Cargo
1761	documents an `edition` on a target that **defaults to** `package.edition` when
1762	absent — `cargo metadata` lists `targets[].edition` and states the package value
1763	is a default individual targets may differ from, and the `[[bin]]`/`[lib]`
1764	`edition` field, though deprecated, is still documented. So *source → package →
1765	package edition* misses a supported override, and a universe whose package
1766	defaults **all agree** can still contain a target that does not. There is
1767	therefore **no single-edition fast path**: a `clones` fact over a Rust universe
1768	requires the committed ownership relation whatever the package map looks like,
1769	and a null `sourceUnitOwnershipId` admits no clone.
1770	
1771	`SourceUnitOwnershipV1` is that relation **and the explicit selection**, and
1772	`RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId` is the `h-identity` of
1773	`native.source-unit-ownership.v1` that carries it — required and nullable,
1774	exactly as `preparedOutputSetId` is. It holds three things:
1775	
1776	- `units` — the **closed table of compilation targets**:
1777	  `{unitId, markerPath, crateName, targetKind, targetName, targetEdition}`.
1778	  `targetEdition` is the target's own edition when it sets one and `null` when it
1779	  takes the package default, so the two committed places can never contradict.
1780	- `selectedUnitIds` — the **explicit analysis scope**, non-empty, every member a
1781	  declared `unitId`.
1782	- `ownership` — the pure relation `{path, unitId}`, carrying no edition and no
1783	  metadata, so it cannot contradict the table.
1784	
1785	`unitId` is **derived, never declared**:
1786	
1787	```
1788	unitId = H(native.compilation-unit.v1,
1789	           UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion: 1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName})
1790	```
1791	
1792	carried as `sha256:<64 hex>`, with **`derived` retention**: nothing separate is
1793	retained, because the preimage *is* the unit row, and admission re-derives and
1794	compares (`sourceUnitOwnership.unitId`). **This is not an opaque digest** — the
1795	preimage record, its domain, its codec and its selector are all published here,
1796	so any consumer rebuilds it from the row that carries it.
1797	
1798	An earlier draft joined the fields with delimiters,
1799	`markerPath#targetKind:targetName`. **That is withdrawn.** It was injective only
1800	by excluding `#` from `markerPath`, and a `#` in a repository directory is
1801	admissible under the canonical repository-path contract — so the recipe narrowed
1802	admitted paths in order to make a delimiter work, which is the wrong trade. `H`
1803	needs no such restriction, is fixed width for every admitted path and name
1804	length, and a marker under a `#`-containing directory closes a complete Run.
1805	
1806	`units` is strictly unique by `unitId`, and `unitId` is a function of the
1807	metadata, so **two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal, never
1808	two units that differ by accident**, and a selection or ownership row naming an
1809	undeclared `unitId` is an unbound caller label and inadmissible.
1810	
1811	`markerPath` is the inventoried manifest that declares the target — the same
1812	vocabulary `WorkspaceUnitV2` already uses, under the ordinary canonical
1813	repository-path admission with no added restriction. **`WorkspaceUnitV2` and
1814	`UnitMembershipV1` cannot supply this binding**, and that is a granularity
1815	statement rather than an oversight: they identify *workspace* units
1816	(`cargo-package`, `cargo-workspace`), while one package holds several targets
1817	that may carry different editions. Naming the marker joins my targets to that
1818	existing discovery vocabulary instead of competing with it.
1819	
1820	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
1821	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
1822	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
1823	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is
1824	validly analysed **under each selection, one at a time**, each with its own
1825	correct dialect and its own body identity, and **no relation payload changed** to
1826	make it so.
1827	
1828	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
1829	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
1830	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
1831	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
1832	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
1833	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
1834	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose
1835	effective editions **agree** are admissible — the ordinary shared-file and
1836	lib-plus-test-target case. Selected owners that **disagree** are an ambiguous
1837	unselected request and refuse. §2.1's retained-input admission independently
1838	requires every marker and owned path to be a source of the same snapshot, every
1839	selection and ownership row to name a declared unit, and every deferring unit to
1840	name a crate the same `edition` map declares.
1841	
1842	**Selected scope is not incomplete enumeration.** A selection says these targets
1843	*are* the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope; it is
1844	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.
1845	`partial` says the producer did not finish, so an owner *inside* the selected
1846	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
1847	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
1848	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
1849	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.
1850	Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run —
1851	the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness,
1852	and the predicate and seal are indeterminate.
1853	
1854	The consequence is the one that matters: an **ordinary mixed-edition workspace
1855	has a representable valid form**. Each path is owned by units of one edition, so
1856	bodies of *both* editions are admissible in the *same* universe, each carrying
1857	its own dialect. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions
1858	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.
1859	This record states what a producer claims it enumerated; it admits no compiler,
1860	measures no build and qualifies no enumerator.
1861	
1862	Exact typed admission precedes every schema check and is imported, not
1863	reimplemented: `canonical.parse` refuses `1.0`, `1e0`, `-0`, non-finite tokens,
1864	duplicate keys and lone surrogates; `canonical.validate` uses the exact-const /
1865	exact-enum / exact-integer validator so `true` is never an integer and `1.0` is
1866	never `1` (`float-spelled-integer-refused`). Every native record schema is closed
1867	(`additionalProperties:false`, checked by the report's `openObjects=[]`).
1868	
1869	---
1870	
1871	## 12. Reference evidence
1872	
1873	`native/native-cases.v2.json` (132 cases) carries hand-authored expected outcomes; every
1874	observation a provider, adapter or OS would make is marked as a trusted observation input.
1875	`native/check_native_evidence.v2.py` verifies every consumed source pin in
1876	`native/source-pins.v2.json` (including the foundation serializer and schemas and the three
1877	workflow schema documents), validates fixtures under exact typed admission (native records
1878	against the closed bundle, 100 definitions; workflow payloads and wrapper records against
1879	the pinned workflow documents through a registry closure, no network), runs the model,
1880	validates the matrix, and writes `native/native-evidence-report.v2.json`.
1881	The identity vectors pin a hand-spelled canonical preimage and use `hashlib` as
1882	the independent oracle; `foundationIdentityVector` does the same for a foundation-domain
1883	identity, so the `subjectScopeCommitment` recipe (§4.1a) is checked against `hashlib`
1884	rather than against the model that produced it. Coverage is reported per item F1–F12,
1885	R1–R7, the post-reset items `PR-MUST-3`, `PR-SHOULD-4`, `PR2-P3`, `PR2-P22`, and the
1886	blind-consumer items `CB-M1`, `CB-M2`, `CB-A1`, `CB-A2`.
1887	
1888	Nothing here executes a compiler, a provider, Cargo, or a repository. Product
1889	behavior on any platform remains qualification work.
1890	
1891	---
1892	
1893	## 13. Joins (closed; current spellings, no future owner choices)
1894	
1895	- **H-1 (foundation, DR-103) — closed.** The security/foundation owners decide the
1896	  repository boundary (`vcs-default`/`cwd-default`/`config`, nested config as a
1897	  deliberate boundary) and trust; inside it this
1898	  contract's `discover_units`/`assign_membership` (§1.4) produce `WorkspaceUnitV2`
1899	  and `UnitMembershipV1`, and `unit_scope_descriptor` emits the foundation
1900	  `scope-descriptor` whose raw digest is the shared `scopeDigest`. Config2
1901	  `discovery` fields are consumed exactly as §1.4 states. Both instruments
1902	  consume the one shared discovery rule
1903	  (`docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`: pruned trees by
1904	  segment, first-party cap, `.` sentinel normalization, the boundary prefix
1905	  rule `classify_boundary` and the inventory conversion
1906	  `boundary_inventory_from_provenance`); a host composition
1907	  calls `enumerate_units(markerRelPaths)` and `classify_path(relPath,
1908	  cargoRoots)` from it rather than restating either, and obtains the boundary
1909	  inventory only from security (U-8).
1910	- **H-8 (security S3, post-reset v2 N-1) — closed.** The authority boundary is
1911	  security's decision; this instrument consumes its `AdmittedBoundaryInventoryV1`
1912	  exactly as U-8 states, yields security's unit set over the same marker
1913	  inventory, and refuses an inventory that was not produced over that inventory.
1914	  **The integration join is implemented, not owed.** `integration-host-model.py`
1915	  `admit_repository_discovery` runs security `discovery` → `DD.boundary_inventory_from_provenance`
1916	  → `N.discover_units(markers, explicit, boundaries)` → `assign_membership` →
1917	  `unit_scope_descriptor`, and `check-integration.py` asserts it on a
1918	  nested-repository/nested-project fixture (`host-nested-boundaries-admitted-once`,
1919	  `-no-native-units`, `-no-source-capture`, `-plan-visible`,
1920	  `host-native-inventory-substitution-refused`,
1921	  `host-launch-inside-nested-config-selects-that-project`), beside the equal-unit-roots and
1922	  equal-pruned-trees checks (`security-native-shared-unit-roots`,
1923	  `security-native-shared-pruned-trees`) and the security sweep
1924	  `admitted-boundary-inventory-joins-security-discovery-and-native-unit-discovery`. Nothing
1925	  is open here. Those files are Codex-owned, so this unit records the join and does not
1926	  restate it.
1927	- **H-2 (security S10) — closed.** Principal class `repository-code` is registered
1928	  by S10 with execution classes `build-script | proc-macro | test-runner`; its
1929	  semantic-grant kind is `trusted-repository-code` and its workflow spelling is
1930	  `P-TRUSTED-REPO` (§5.1, schema constants). Enforcement values in
1931	  `AuthorizedExecutionV2.effects` are copied from the pinned
1932	  `permission-truth-tables.v9.json` and must equal S10's entries; the revocation
1933	  clock is consulted `before-each-owner`; cancellation is `process-group-kill`.
1934	  If an enforced primitive is later measured on a platform, only that value changes.
1935	- **H-3 (host D9) — closed.** No new deficiency enum members and no new reason
1936	  codes are requested. Native deficiencies are typed detail inside the coverage2
1937	  record named by the termination's `coverageId`; the D9 codes used are exactly
1938	  the existing `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE`, `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`,
1939	  `COVERAGE.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`,
1940	  `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`, `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (§10).
1941	- **H-4 (host error codes) — closed.** Withdrawn: preparation bounds and ambient
1942	  config are `HOST.IO_FAILURE` with the native detail strings; no
1943	  `NATIVE.*` codes exist.
1944	- **H-5 (workflow) — closed.** Import payloads: one canonical schema document per
1945	  kind (§7.1); wrapper digests: the workflow `ImportWrapperV2` raw-SHA recipe
1946	  (§7.2); correspondence/mapping: the workflow `SourceCorrespondence` +
1947	  `SourceMappingV1` (§7.3). `native.prepare` and import are workflow operational
1948	  steps with the workflow's CLI spelling and receipts; inert prepared/imported
1949	  blobs are host CAS objects under the storage custody rules (§1.4). The workflow
1950	  repair prerequisites consume `ClosedWorldV2.deadCodeRepairEligible` and
1951	  `affected_targets` as stated in §4.5; HTML/agent projections render
1952	  `resolutionCompleteness` and disclosures verbatim.
1953	- **H-6 (Codex identity) — unchanged.** The reference model imports Codex's
1954	  serializer and `import2` identifier by file; if those bytes change, this unit
1955	  re-pins and re-runs; no native serializer exists to diverge.
1956	- **Formerly recorded conflicts — both resolved in current bytes:** (a) §7.4 —
1957	  the workflow `build_import` now uses raw SHA-256 auxiliary digests and one
1958	  payload domain per kind (verified by the integration wrapper-equality checks);
1959	  (b) the security S10 text and the security model's S10 section comment now
1960	  name `AuthorizedExecutionV2` (same effect values). No conflict is open.
1961	- **H-7 (security S10, post-reset SHOULD-2) — closed.** Grant admission is
1962	  operational and precedes any Plan; the principals a consuming analysis must
1963	  project for `preparedResolution=host-prepared` are exactly
1964	  `semantic_projection_for_grants(consumed preparation grants)`, checked at
1965	  Plan admission by `admit_plan_execution_projection`; `imported-inert`
1966	  projects none (§5.1 unchanged); a test-runner grant is projected by nothing.
1967	- **Disagreement statement:** none with the coordinating proposals. One
1968	  retained refinement: the joint text says an incomplete Rust universe "produces
1969	  Coverage provider-unavailable"; this contract types it
1970	  `input-closure-incomplete` (the remedy differs) and carries it as typed detail
1971	  under the existing `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE`, which changes no vocabulary owned by
1972	  another unit.
1973	
1974	## 14. Host composition corrections (mixed authorship; independent Claude review pending)
1975	
1976	`AuthorizedExecutionV2` is a preparation preflight descriptor, not a security
1977	admission result. `opensip native prepare --authorization PATH --grant-set PATH`
1978	selects its retained canonical bytes and operational grant set. PATH inputs receive
1979	ordinary user-input custody checks. The invocation contains a `native-preparation`
1980	step with `authorizationDescriptorDigest` (raw SHA-256) and `securityGrantSetRef`.
1981	The host verifies those preimages before admission. A completed step returns an
1982	execution receipt and one admitted prepared import, never a Run. Execution is never
1983	an automatic retry; cancellation kills the admitted process group and retains an
1984	indeterminate journal if completion cannot be established. A new explicit request
1985	is required to repeat interrupted execution. Inspection of the journal executes
1986	nothing. Publication of prepared evidence requires complete output admission and
1987	current source correspondence; an execution receipt alone does not supply evidence.
1988	
1989	Each preparation owner has an explicit `source` (snapshot-member or
1990	dependency-closure-member) and receives one class-specific RepoExecutionGrantV2.
1991	The preparation bound is 4096 owners; this composes as up to 4096 single-owner
1992	grants and does not enlarge security's 64-owner per-grant bound. Each grant binds
1993	the actual host-selected argv/runner, class, project, snapshot, platform, tool and
1994	dependency closures, consent and effect disclosure. Every grant is admitted through
1995	security's complete schema and decision model before any spawn, with live boundaries
1996	rechecked during execution. Native preflight success alone cannot authorize a spawn.
1997	
1998	An owner's semantic source preimage is the canonical singleton array of the closed
1999	security row `{ownerKey,source,ownerFileManifestSha256}`. Its raw SHA-256 is
2000	ownerSourceDigest in both the semantic principal and that owner's operational
2001	grant. The preimage is retained. Multi-owner security grants use the same record
2002	array sorted by unique ownerKey. `securityGrantSetRef` is
2003	`security.repo-execution-grants.v2:` plus H over
2004	`{schemaVersion:2,grantRefs:sortedUniqueV2GrantRefs}`. The actual per-grant reference
2005	is `security.repo-execution-grant.v2:` plus H of the admitted grant. These operational
2006	references and consent are excluded from the semantic Plan.
2007	
2008	Native-context schema 2's `typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` and `rustcDevLlvmDigest`
2009	join foundation's exact stdlib/rust-dev-llvm closure2 suffix recipes, with complete
2010	admitted descriptors and trees retained. Their exact locations are
2011	`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` (§2.4) and
2012	`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest` (§2.3), each inside its language's
2013	toolchain-identity record; `admit_native_context` performs the re-prefix-and-recompute join
2014	against the retained closure. Manifest digests hash the security metadata
2015	body encoding, excluding its signature envelope. Subject discriminators use the
2016	canonical declaration-signature string-array preimage from identity §3; bodies,
2017	positions and encounter-order suffixes are excluded, and duplicate signatures in a
2018	collision class refuse correspondence. The reference adapter exercises this hash
2019	join; actual compiler token projection remains a named native qualification task.
2020	
2021	The discovery instrument can enumerate 4096 first-party units (installed
2022	dependency manifests are pruned first and never count, §1.4 U-4a/U-7), while an
2023	admitted foundation scope permits at most 1024 selected workspace roots. The
2024	effective scope limit is 1024; overflow refuses without truncation and asks for a
2025	narrower explicit scope. Discovery's larger diagnostic population does not bypass
2026	the analysis input bound. A workspace root `.` names the already admitted project
2027	root under the shared `normalize_explicit_root` (§1.4).
2028	
2029	Near-clone groups are connected components of threshold-passing edges.
2030	`matchedEdges` exposes the actual endpoint IDs and each Jaccard score;
2031	`scoreMeaning=minimum-member-best-neighbor` describes the group summary score.
2032	It does not claim that every pair in the component passes the threshold. Normal
2033	canonical record-size and work budgets still apply; exceeding them is explicit
2034	incomplete analysis, never an undisclosed truncation. Reviewed candidate identities
2035	follow a stable source fingerprint within a project, separately from the current
2036	Run, under the workflow review contract.
2037	
2038	Cross-unit reference evidence: `docs/coop/design-corrections/integration-host-model.py`
2039	and `check-integration.py`. The model composes actual reference admissions over
2040	synthetic TCB inputs; it does not execute repository code or measure confinement.
2041	
2042	Public details for the shared cap and explicit-root grammar are PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT and PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID. The pure instrument retains native.too-many-units and native.explicit-root-grammar only as internal aliases; the host normalizes them through public-detail-registry.v1.json, and the public schema rejects those aliases. The internal capability table key provider-unavailable/capability-missing emits native.capability-unavailable publicly.
2043	
2044	The four repository-code child-process effect selections in §5 are consistent with the accepted permission-truth-tables.v9 head. The v7→v9 changes concern metadata/recording and the host-under-instruction network recital; the permission table rows supplying the four selections are unchanged. The product still declares these as its own supported-platform design selections, not measured confinement or an extension of preview qualification.
2045	
2046	
2047	A scope array that exceeds the shared foundation schema bound refuses REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE (request-rejected, exit2), public detail PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT and subject `field:count>limit`; it is never truncated. workspaceRoots has limit1024 (distinct roots after co-located unit deduplication), and pathPrefixes/excludedPathPrefixes each65536. Thus1025..4096 valid discovered unit roots produce this typed scope refusal, while more than4096 first-party unit directories produce PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT earlier. The public code is shared across host/native scope admission; callers must narrow explicit selection. Native ScopeRefusal retains detail, D9 and observed bound fields for the host's closed termination projection.
2048	
2049	The standalone boundary-crossing key native.explicit-root-crosses-boundary is an internal alias of PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID, the code security emits before native on the operational path. native.boundary-inventory-mismatch is an internal alias of PROJECT.DISCOVERY_INVENTORY_MISMATCH. The latter public condition is emitted by the actual host when its native marker/file inventory disagrees with the security discovery inventory (REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED, exit2), including before native is invoked. Neither internal spelling is a public enum value.

62	## 1. Invocation, step, attempt, Run (AR-08)
63	
64	An invocation is one host request. Its operational identity is `RequestId`, minted
65	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. The invocation is an
66	ordered acyclic list of at most **64 steps**; `StepId` is the zero-based position.
67	Each admitted attempt of a step receives a fresh `ExecutionId`; a step has at most
68	**3 attempts**. Only `analysis` and `verify` steps seal or link a content-derived
69	`run2`. `comparison`, `query`, `render`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`,
70	`test-execution`, `native-preparation`, `mutation`, `export-delivery` and `doctor` are operational steps
71	that never mint a Run. Schema: `invocation-record.schema.json`.
72	
73	**Step DAG versus derivation DAG.** The step list is the operational workflow. Each
74	analysis/verify *attempt* owns exactly one derivation DAG (`exec-plan2`, at most
75	**1024 stages**) recorded in the attempt's `derivation` binding
76	(`planId`, `executionPlanId`, `stageCount`, `stagesCompleted`, `firstFailedStage`).
77	A step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. A retry on
78	identical admitted inputs may bind the same `exec-plan2` and the same Run; attempts
79	remain separately auditable.
80	
81	**Dependencies.** `dependsOn` names lower StepIds only (a forward or self reference is
82	`WORKFLOW.DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, request-rejected). `requirement` is `required` or
83	`optional`; a required step may not depend on an optional step
84	(`WORKFLOW.REQUIRED_DEPENDS_ON_OPTIONAL`). `dependencyGate` is `completed` (every
85	dependency completed) or `terminal` (every dependency reached any terminal outcome;
86	lawful only for `render`/`export-delivery`, which project whatever happened). A
87	step whose gate is unmet is `skipped` with a typed `skipReason`. Step outcomes are
88	closed: `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`
89	(crash recovery only).
90	
91	**Retries.** `retryPolicy=idempotent-retry` is lawful only for `analysis`, `verify`,
92	`query`, `render`, `doctor` and `export-delivery`, only for `faultCause=ledger-busy`,
93	and within the 3-attempt budget; exhausting it is `LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT` (4) with
94	detail `WORKFLOW.RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. `host-io` and every other fault are never
95	retried. `mutation`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`, `comparison`, `native-preparation` and `test-execution`
96	carry `retryPolicy=none` by schema; a spec violating this is refused.
97	
98	**Mutation idempotence and recovery.** Generic `mutation` steps use the bare
99	64-hex `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)`. The closed retained
100	scope is exactly `{schemaVersion:1,requestId,stepId,projectId,operation}`, with
101	`operation` equal to `MutationParams.mutationClass`. This explicitly succeeds the
102	former undefined `{operation,projectId,effect preimage}` description. The key is
103	operational and scoped to one host-minted request and admitted immutable step;
104	different fresh requests never deduplicate each other's generic mutations.
105	`sourceStep` resolves inside that same retained invocation, whose admitted
106	parameters and completed dependency results are immutable. Before lookup or
107	replay the host validates the scope and full params, recomputes the key and
108	requires the retained invocation/project/step/operation binding; a caller cannot
109	nominate another invocation's scope or change effect inputs under an old key.
110	Receipt lookup is never an effect-authorization mechanism. A same-scope COMPLETED
111	receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect. Failure, unknown state or
112	incomplete execution requires the operation's existing recovery law, not blind
113	re-execution. Recovery started in a new request retains its own operational scope
114	and the explicit original journal/intent links required by §§6/12.
115	
116	Repair apply is the explicit content-derived exception: it is a dedicated
117	`repair-apply` step, excluded from generic MutationParams. It uses the raw SHA-256 of
118	canonical `{operation:"repair-apply",projectId,repairPlanId,baseSnapshotId}` as its
119	idempotency key. An equal completed key performs no second effect. The original
120	receipt is immutable; a replay delivery produces a separately identified receipt
121	with the new request/attempt binding and `replayed=true`. Mutation receipts use
122	`receipt2:` plus `H('workflow.mutation-receipt', receiptWithoutReceiptId)` and remain
123	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
124	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
125	
126	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
127	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
128	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
129	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
130	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
131	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
132	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
133	
134	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
135	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
136	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
137	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
138	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
139	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
140	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
141	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
142	
143	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
144	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
145	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
146	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
147	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
148	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
149	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
150	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
151	
152	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
153	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
154	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
155	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
156	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
157	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
158	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
159	
160	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
161	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
162	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
163	No policy file is written implicitly.

167	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)
168	
169	`BaselineArtifactV1` lives in the repository as tracked intent
170	(`opensip.baseline.json`). `baselineId = H('workflow.baseline', descriptor)`. The
171	descriptor pins: origin ProjectId, source `snapshot2`, the **authoritative** `run2`
172	and `plan2` (an ephemeral result is refused: `BASELINE.SOURCE_EPHEMERAL`), the
173	fingerprint recipe (`finding-fingerprint`, major ≥ 2), every contributing detector's
174	`closure2` with semantics major, the complete **pivot closure** (detector executable,
175	evaluator, toolchain/stdlib, schema set; each a `closure2` with manifest digest,
176	protocol major and platform), the evaluation context digests, the **embedded**
177	policy/scope/waiver documents whose digests equal those context digests, rule
178	coverage, and sorted unique entries. Custody (outside identity) carries host release,
179	export time, `retentionPins` (the Run and every pivot closure) and an optional signed
180	`closureBundle` reference.
181	
182	**Fresh CI.** Comparison never reads the origin machine's store. A fresh host admits
183	the artifact by recomputing `baselineId`, checking schema major, recipe major,
184	sortedness, context-document digests and project correspondence (same ProjectId, or
185	explicit `--accept-origin`, else `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` and no comparison). It
186	resolves each pivot closure from (a) a retained generation, (b) an installed signed
187	release with the same `closure2`, or (c) the signed closure bundle; all under
188	**current trust**. A closure that is missing (`pivot-detector-unavailable`), revoked
189	(`pivot-closure-revoked`) or incompatible with the host's protocol majors/platform
190	(`pivot-closure-incompatible`) makes E0 unavailable; a revoked closure is never
191	executed, whatever bytes are present.
192	
193	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison
194	is lawful only when the closures are identical (`identical-closure`) or the current
195	detector's signed manifest lists the baseline `closure2` as exactly semantically
196	compatible at the same major (`declared-compatible`). Otherwise the baseline detector
197	must run over current source (`three-way-pivot`, an authoritative pivot analysis step
198	planned before the primary one) or the detector's entries are `INDETERMINATE`.
199	Fingerprint dual emission (`legacyFingerprint`) migrates identity only and never
200	supplies the prior algorithm. Adoption pins the Run and the pivot closures as
201	retention roots; loss of a pin is disclosed as partial availability and yields typed
202	indeterminacy, never a silent two-way fallback. `baseline-upgrade` re-adopts under the
203	current detector explicitly and is a mutation with its own receipt.

207	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
208	
209	`ComparisonResultV1` (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
210	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
211	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
212	
213	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
214	|---|---|---|---|---|
215	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
216	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
217	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
218	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
219	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
220	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
221	
222	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
223	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
224	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
225	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
226	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
227	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
228	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
229	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
230	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
231	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
232	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
233	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
234	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
235	
236	**Detector union.** Comparison covers the union of baseline and current detectors.
237	Added detectors set E0 false. Removed detectors require the actual current-trusted
238	prior detector pivot and set E1–E4 false; E0 must never be substituted with B.
239	Consequently a new bug hidden by removing its detector remains CODE-NET-NEW and
240	can gate. Missing prior execution is indeterminate, including detector removal.
241	
242	**Evidence axis.** Compare the exact bound `import2` identity sets per kind, with
243	payload/correspondence/scope/observation digests retained in each BoundImport.
244	Replacing an artifact with another of the same kind is still an evidence change
245	(`evidence-content-changed`). For a rule with declared `evidenceUse`: if required evidence is
246	absent on the current side the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
247	(`required-evidence-unavailable`) and the rule's coverage is unsatisfied; if
248	availability changed and the rule gates on either side, attribution is
249	`INDETERMINATE` (`evidence-availability-changed`); only for a non-gating rule may a
250	presence change be `EVIDENCE-DELTA`. Required evidence loss can never disappear as a
251	non-gating delta.
252	
253	**Audit profiles select gate semantics explicitly** (schema `AuditProfile`):
254	
255	| Profile | Gates CODE-NET-NEW | Gates newly live via policy/scope/waiver | Gates all current live | New waiver suppresses net-new | Rule gating under |
256	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
257	| `code-regression` (default for `audit`) | yes | no | no | no | baseline or current |
258	| `policy-change` | yes | yes | no | no | baseline or current |
259	| `full-current` | yes | yes | yes | yes | current only |
260	| `report-only` | no | no | no | yes | current only |
261	
262	A `CODE-NET-NEW` entry that is not live in current (hidden by a later policy/scope
263	change or by a waiver added in the same change) still gates under
264	`baseline-or-current` with `gateReason=code-net-new-policy-hidden`. Verdict is `fail`
265	if any entry gates, else `indeterminate` if any `INDETERMINATE` entry belongs to a
266	gating rule or a current gating rule has unsatisfied/unknown required Coverage or
267	evidence, else `pass`. Rule deficiencies are enumerated independently of findings;
268	zero emitted findings never establish complete analysis. Whole-comparison indeterminacy (unmapped project,
269	unsupported schema/recipe major, context document mismatch) performs no comparison
270	and emits zero entries with a typed remedy. Enum precedence never decides a gate.

274	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
275	
276	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
277	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
278	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
279	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
280	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
281	
282	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
283	|---|---|---|
284	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
285	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
286	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
287	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
288	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
289	
290	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
291	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
292	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
293	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
294	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
295	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
296	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
297	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
298	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
299	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
300	
301	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
302	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
303	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
304	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
305	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
306	
307	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
308	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
309	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
310	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
311	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
312	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
313	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
314	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
315	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
316	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
317	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
318	but never feeds a predicate.
319	
320	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
321	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive
322	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
323	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
324	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
325	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
326	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.

330	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
331	
332	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV1` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
333	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
334	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
335	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
336	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
337	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
338	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
339	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
340	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
341	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
342	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
343	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
344	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
345	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
346	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
347	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
348	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
349	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
350	The compiled RuleProgramV1 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
351	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
352	
353	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
354	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
355	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
356	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
357	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
358	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
359	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
360	
361	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
362	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
363	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
364	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
365	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
366	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
367	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
368	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
369	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
370	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
371	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
372	
373	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
374	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
375	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
376	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
377	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
378	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
379	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
380	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
381	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
382	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
383	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
384	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
385	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.

389	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
390	
391	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
392	
393	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
394	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
395	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
396	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
397	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
398	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
399	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
400	`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
401	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
402	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
403	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
404	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
405	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
406	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
407	
408	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
409	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
410	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
411	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
412	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
413	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
414	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
415	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
416	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
417	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
418	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
419	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
420	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.

426	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,

431	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
432	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.

A recovery segment may begin in any closed state; it must bind that starting reference, retain the same admitted intent/registry/scope, and follow the state table. This gives PREPARED→COMMITTED→DONE recovery a representable independent history while the original attempt remains LEASED→PREPARING→PREPARED.

774	
775	| Security consent.mode | TestExecutionStepParams.consentSource | RepairApplyParams.consentSource |
776	|---|---|---|
777	| interactive-explicit | interactive-consent | interactive |
778	| policy-record | pre-existing-policy | policy |

780	These field-specific spellings do not define independent authorization mechanisms. Test and repair projections carry the mapped source, and repair additionally carries the admitted CI observation; their workflow mechanics require exact equality with the selected step/context. Interactive consent refuses in CI at security admission. Policy-record consent is valid both in CI and outside CI when the actual policy admission succeeds. Relabelling an admitted grant's source is refused. A completed idempotent repair replay performs no mutation; it returns the existing receipt under the existing replay contract.

56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are
123	discovered **automatically** for the zero-config full product, with precedence:
124	
125	| Source | Provenance `unitSource` | Custody failure |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| repeatable CLI `--workspace-root PATH` overrides | `explicit-joins` | refuses (explicit intent) |
128	| admitted Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots` (foundation product-configuration schema v2) | `config-workspace-roots` | refuses |
129	| marker scan of the admitted root | `automatic` | unit excluded, recorded in `excludedUnits` with the reason |
130	
131	An explicit source suppresses automatic discovery. Every directory from the
132	root to a unit must pass directory custody and stay inside the root (no
133	absolute, `.`, `..`, backslash or NUL segments); every marker file must pass
134	file custody. A manifest is **data**: discovery records its presence and later
135	readers parse it as data only, never running scripts, hooks, plugins or
136	workspace globs and never writing source.
137	
138	**One shared discovery rule (MUST-3).** The zero-config rule is stated once, in
139	`docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by this
140	instrument and by the native unit instrument (native §1.4); neither restates
141	it. Before any custody walk, automatic discovery prunes, by **exact path
142	segment** (never substring): dependency trees (a segment `node_modules`), VCS
143	trees (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`) and Cargo build output (a segment
144	`target` whose parent directory holds `Cargo.toml`, an actual Cargo root; a
145	source directory merely called `target`, such as `packages/target` or
146	`src/target`, is ordinary source). A pruned tree yields no unit, no marker,
147	no custody walk and no program member; its anchor is recorded **once** in
148	`prunedTrees` with the number of markers it hid, so 4200 installed package
149	manifests are one record, never 4200 units. A `Cargo.toml` inside a pruned
150	tree does not create a Cargo root. First-party unit directories are capped at

152	`REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, detail `WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT:<n>><cap>`) with no
153	truncation; installed dependencies never count toward it (checker sweep
154	`discovery-prunes-installed-dependencies-and-refuses-real-cap-typed`: 4200
155	installed manifests admit with one unit; 4200 first-party directories refuse;

158	**Explicit roots are exact roots.** CLI `--workspace-root` and Config2
159	`discovery.workspaceRoots` values are normalized by the shared
160	`normalize_explicit_root`: `.` alone denotes the admitted project root
161	(identity-and-evidence §3 sentinel; internal root ``, the same value the native

167	and any other empty, `.`, `..`,
168	absolute, backslash or NUL segment is `JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`. An explicit root
169	inside a pruned tree refuses `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE:<reason>:<anchor>`. An
170	explicit root **without a language marker** is admitted here for custody (unit

177	Custody-excluded units are explicit unknown required scope, not a successful

184	**Pruned trees and the read set (A-5).** "No custody walk" for a pruned tree

242	## S4. Trust time (AR-04)
243	
244	Definitions. `evalHighWater` (floor F): highest instant at which a decision
245	evaluation was made. `lastAccepted` (L): issue time of the newest accepted
246	signed document; required whenever F exists. **Admitted time evidence** A =
247	max(L, accepted witness time, presented root issue time), where a witness is
248	the newest issue time of a presented payload whose signature already verified
249	and which is not older than L. The wall clock is untrusted.
250	
251	Decision evaluation, in order, for record R, observation (wall W, sleep-
252	inclusive monotonic M, bootId B), optional payload P:
253	
254	1. Payload future check (unchanged FC-FUTURE): an issue time > W + 24 h refuses
255	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`; nothing is written.
256	2. Fresh install (F absent): without admitted time evidence the evaluation
257	   refuses `TRUST.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (the core's embedded bootstrap
258	   payload or an ordinary payload is required); nothing is written. With it,
259	   W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` and initialises nothing.
260	   Otherwise tEval = max(W, A); F := tEval, L := A, anchor := (B, M, W); expiry
261	   states are evaluated from the presented documents, never set to false.
262	3. In-session continuity: if the anchor has the same bootId, expected =
263	   anchorWall + (M − anchorMono). A forward deviation over 24 h refuses
264	   `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` (`in-session`) unless a witness proves the
265	   expectation itself was behind (witness ≥ expected). A backward deviation is
266	   the finding `CLOCK-REGRESSION-IN-SESSION`; a monotonic value below the
267	   anchor's is `CLOCK-CONTINUITY-MALFORMED` (finding, anchor not rewritten).
268	4. Plausibility: W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD`
269	   (`beyond-horizon`) **before any evaluation and before any write**. Remedy:
270	   correct the clock, or present a payload issued within 90 d of W.
271	5. Evaluation: tEval = max(F, W, A). The floor written is exactly tEval
272	   (write-ahead, §5.6 durability), so the persisted floor and the evaluated
273	   instant never differ and no later evaluation runs earlier than an earlier
274	   one. `CLOCK-REGRESSION` (W < F) and `TRUST.FLOOR_AHEAD_OF_WALL`
275	   (F > W + 90 d) are findings with remedies. L advances to A when A > L. The
276	   anchor is rewritten when continuity is unavailable, within tolerance, or
277	   excused by a witness.
278	
279	Consequences. An accidental forward wall is accepted only up to 90 d beyond
280	signed evidence, so a wrong write is bounded and heals as signed time catches
281	up; a larger jump writes nothing. Expiry, staleness and future checks still
282	fail closed at tEval. Repeated reboots cannot lower F or freeze payload
283	freshness: F only rises, and freshness is evaluated at tEval ≥ F. Report-only
284	evaluation (doctor) computes the same decision, states and findings, labels
285	`evaluationMode: report-only`, and returns `writes: []` with every write field
286	null; it cannot create a recovery challenge.
287	
288	### S4.5 Recovery of an already poisoned floor
289	
290	A floor years ahead of real time (written by the superseded rule, or by a
291	restore) cannot be lowered by ordinary payloads: tEval ≥ F keeps every document
292	expired. Recovery is an authenticated, install-bound, single-use act:
293	
294	1. `opensip trust recovery-challenge` (decision mode only; global fence, no
295	   project lease) writes one pending challenge and exports
296	   `trust-recovery-challenge.v1.json` (`TrustRecoveryChallengeV1`): a fresh
297	   32-byte host-CSPRNG nonce, `createdWall`, and `recordDigest` =
298	   metadata-profile digest, domain `opensip.metadata.recovery-challenge.1`,
299	   over the six bound fields `{evalHighWater, lastAccepted, rootVersion,
300	   revocationVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, recoveryEpochSerial}`. The
301	   pending record additionally binds `{bootId, createdMono, expiresMono =
302	   createdMono + 24 h, createdWall}` with sleep-inclusive monotonic time. A
303	   new challenge replaces the pending one; a reboot invalidates it.
304	2. The publisher's recovery service (consented online) or the air-gap ceremony
305	   returns `trust-recovery-epoch.v1.json`: an `opensip-signature-envelope.2`
306	   of kind `trust-recovery-epoch` (digest domain
307	   `opensip.metadata.recovery-epoch.1`) with body `TrustRecoveryEpochV1`
308	   `{recoverySchema:1, kind, epochSerial, issuedAt, challenge{nonce,
309	   recordDigest}, counters{rootVersion, revocationVersion,
310	   indexSnapshotVersion}, installBinding:"challenge"}`. Authority is the
311	   **accepted root's `recoveryAuthority.keys` at `recoveryAuthority.threshold`**
312	   (the existing schema-1 field: 5–16 keys, threshold ≥ 3, disjoint from
313	   `rootKeys`), revoked keys excluded. Root keys never count, so routine
314	   recovery never exercises root keys and root-key compromise alone cannot
315	   lower a floor. The accepted root's expiry is not consulted for this one
316	   document because the floor under repair is what expired it. This is the
317	   only external artifact needed.
318	3. `opensip trust recovery-import` verifies, under the global fence and no
319	   project lease, in this order: (a) **strict closed shape of the epoch and of
320	   the pending record before any comparison** (exact-typed constants: `true`
321	   is never `1`, integers are never booleans, timestamps by grammar, hex by
322	   grammar); (b) recovery-authority threshold; (c) a pending challenge exists,
323	   its `bootId` equals the current boot, and `createdMono ≤ mono ≤
324	   expiresMono` (`CHALLENGE_BOOT_CHANGED`, `CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`,
325	   `CHALLENGE_CONTINUITY_MALFORMED`); (d) nonce equals the pending nonce;
326	   `recordDigest` equals both the pending value and a fresh digest of the
327	   current record; `epochSerial` > `recoveryEpochSerial`; (e) **every counter
328	   equals the challenged record's counter exactly** (`COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`).
329	   A higher signed counter is refused with that typed detail; the remedy is to
330	   import the ordinary payload that carries it and re-challenge. Nothing is
331	   silently discarded and nothing is silently advanced. (f) `issuedAt` ≥ L and
332	   |`issuedAt` − W| ≤ 24 h (`ISSUED_IN_FUTURE`, `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`).
333	   Any failure refuses `RECOVERY.REFUSED` with the typed detail and changes
334	   nothing.
335	4. On success: F := L := `issuedAt`; anchor cleared; `recoveryEpochSerial` :=
336	   `epochSerial`; pending challenge consumed; audit record `RECOVERY-EPOCH`
337	   with the previous floor. Counters, revocation entries, role states,
338	   journals and namespaces are untouched; no namespace is deleted.
339	
340	Threat statement. The wall is untrusted. The single-boot, 24 h monotonic
341	challenge window plus the ±24 h issue skew mean that no response to an old
342	challenge, held indefinitely, can later lower the floor to a stale real time:
343	after a reboot or after the window the response is dead, and inside the window
344	the signed time must sit within a day of the wall the operator is looking at.
345	This bounds a signed epoch relative to the wall; it does not prove the wall.
346	The protocol promises install binding (nonce + record digest), single use,
347	serial monotonicity, exact counter preservation and no floor below L. It makes
348	**no promise against a malicious publisher**: a recovery authority that signs a
349	false time is outside the protocol, exactly as it is for every other signed
350	time in this contract. Why this cannot revive revoked trust: revocation is by
351	counter and entries, which the epoch may not change; a key revoked before the
352	epoch cannot sign it; expiry is re-evaluated at signed real time, which is ≥
353	every earlier signed time, so a document genuinely expired at real time stays
354	expired. If the recovery authority is unavailable, recovery is impossible and
355	the install must be re-established by fresh install or authenticated adoption.
356	Migration and rollback (S9) never carry a pending challenge; the serial moves
357	forward with the other floors.
358	
359	## S5. Root chain through expired roots (AR-05)
360	
361	An install holding accepted root N evaluates a chain N+1..M link by link. Each
362	link needs the previous root's threshold from that root's keys (continuity)
363	**and** the new root's threshold from its own keys (possession), revoked keys
364	excluded from both. Semantic admission per link: reader supports the schema;
365	version and previous-version contiguity; not issued before its predecessor;
366	issue before expiry; root key policy. Intermediate expiry is never consulted;
367	the final root must be unexpired at tEval and not issued more than 24 h after
368	the wall. Any refusal leaves state unchanged and names the link. Success
369	advances the root counter to M and L to the final root's issue time. An expired
370	root with no chain refuses `ROOT.EXPIRED_NO_CHAIN` with the remedy of presenting
